question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.
sql:
WITH order_lines AS (
    SELECT product_id, qty as qty_needed
    FROM orderlines
    WHERE order_id = 423
),
inventory_with_date AS (
    SELECT inv.id, inv.product_id, inv.location_id, inv.purchase_id, inv.qty as inv_qty, l.warehouse, l.aisle, l.position, p.purchased
    FROM inventory inv
    JOIN locations l ON inv.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON inv.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
    AND inv.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_lines)
),
ranked_inventory AS (
    SELECT *, 
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, inv_qty) as rn,
           SUM(inv_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, inv_qty ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as cum_qty,
           COALESCE(SUM(inv_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, inv_qty ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), 0) as prev_cum_qty
    FROM inventory_with_date
),
needed AS (
    SELECT product_id, qty_needed FROM order_lines
),
allocated AS (
    SELECT 
        r.product_id,
        r.location_id,
        r.aisle,
        r.position,
        r.inv_qty,
        r.rn,
        n.qty_needed,
        r.prev_cum_qty,
        LEAST(n.qty_needed - r.prev_cum_qty, r.inv_qty) as pick_qty
    FROM ranked_inventory r
    JOIN needed n ON r.product_id = n.product_id
    WHERE r.prev_cum_qty < n.qty_needed
)
SELECT product_id, aisle, position, pick_qty
FROM allocated
ORDER BY product_id, rn
